title: This Robot Dog Just Ran a Marathon — and Beat the Average Human
summary:
Imagine a dog with four metal legs, no fur, and no need for water breaks. That's RAIBO2 — a robot dog built by engineers in South Korea. In 2024, it ran a whole marathon: 26.2 miles through the Sangju Dried Persimmon Marathon. It finished in 4 hours, 19 minutes, and 52 seconds. The average human takes about 4 hours and 32 minutes. So RAIBO2 was faster than most people!

Here's the wild part: it did the whole race on one single battery charge. And when it crossed the finish line, it still had more than a third of its battery left. That's like finishing a huge race and barely being tired.

Why is that a big deal? Robot dogs with legs use lots of energy just standing up and taking steps. Older robot dogs could only go about 12 miles. RAIBO2 went more than double that.

The engineers trained it like a real puppy — rewarding it every time it stepped softly without slipping. A human did steer it with a camera, but RAIBO2 did all the running. Good robot. Have a treat!
why_it_matters: Machines are getting better at hard things humans do, so the sports, jobs and inventions you grow up with may look very different from today's.

background_read: RAIBO2 was built by engineers in South Korea (a country in East Asia) that makes many clever robots and machines.
A marathon is always 26.2 miles long, and the race is named after an old Greek legend about a messenger who ran a very long way to deliver news.
Robot dogs are already used in real life — some walk around factories to check for problems, and some help rescue teams search for people after a disaster.
Article_Structure: WHO: Engineers in South Korea built RAIBO2, a robot dog with four metal legs, and a human steered it during the race using a camera.

WHAT: RAIBO2 ran a full 26.2-mile marathon in 4 hours, 19 minutes and 52 seconds — beating the average human time of about 4 hours 32 minutes — on one single battery charge, and finished with more than a third of the battery left.
WHERE: The Sangju Dried Persimmon Marathon in South Korea.

WHY: Robot dogs with legs waste lots of energy just standing and taking steps, and older ones could only go about 12 miles — RAIBO2 more than doubled that, showing how much better robot stamina has become.

perspectives.description: They think RAIBO2 is amazing proof that robots could one day carry supplies, inspect dangerous places or help in rescues.
Comparing a robot to the AVERAGE human isn't really fair, because the fastest human runners finish a marathon in a little over two hours, far ahead of RAIBO2.
They point out a human still had to steer RAIBO2 with a camera, so the robot did not do everything by itself.
